question: Compare the performance of product X and product Y and explain why they differ.
sql: SELECT p.name, p.brand, p.category, p.department, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(AVG(oi.sale_price - p.cost), 2) AS avg_margin, ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned'), COUNT(*)) * 100, 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE LOWER(p.name) IN ('product x', 'product y') GROUP BY p.name, p.brand, p.category, p.department ORDER BY revenue DESC
report:
**Finding.** Revenue alone is misleading. The higher-revenue product carried a materially worse return rate, so contribution after returns was the lower of the two.

**Driver.** Return rate and unit margin explain the gap far more than order count. Category and brand act as confounders - always report them alongside.

**Recommendation.** Rank product comparisons on margin net of returns, not gross revenue.

**Convention.** A product comparison must always report four measures together: orders, revenue, average unit margin (sale_price - cost) and return rate. Use SAFE_DIVIDE for every ratio so an empty denominator yields NULL instead of an error.
